panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Histology image from enucleated eye of Lowe syndrome patient showing corneal opacification with fibrovascular proliferation in the subepithelial region, consistent with corneal ischemia as described in the caption. B: Histology image showing anterior chamber abnormalities in Lowe syndrome, including dense fibrous tissue covering the angle, peripheral anterior synechiae, ectropion uvea, and iris stromal atrophy. C: Histology image showing an underdeveloped and atrophic ciliary body with peripheral staphyloma in Lowe syndrome. D: Histology image showing optic nerve pathology in Lowe syndrome including loss of retinal ganglion cell layer, retinal gliosis, and glaucomatous cupping of the optic nerve head.

panels.figure_caption: Ocular histopathology analysis of Lowe patient 2. (A) Cornea thickening and scarring with fibrovascular proliferation in the subepithelial region. Scale bar 1 mm. (B) The angle of the anterior chamber is covered in dense fibrous tissues adherent to the cornea and the iris stroma. Extensive ectropion uvea overlay the atropic iris. Scale bar 1 mm. (C) Ciliary body is underdeveloped and atrophic with peripheral staphyloma. Scale bar 0.5 mm. (D) Optic nerve shows loss of retinal ganglion cell layer, retinal gliosis, and cupping of optic nerve head. Scale bar 0.5 mm.
in_text_mentions: enucleated eye, the cornea is completely opacified with extensive fibrovascular proliferation, loss of endothelial cells, and peripheral stromal neovascularization, indicating corneal ischemia (Fig. 2A). The angle of the anterior chamber is covered with dense fibrous tissue with peripheral anterior synchiae. The iris stroma is atrophic with extensive ectropion uvea (Fig. 2B,C). Ciliary body is atrophic with peripheral staphyloma under the area of Ahmed glaucoma drainage implant. Optic nerve shows atrophy and loss of axons and cupping of optic nerve head (Fig. 2D). findings.label: Congenital cataract
findings.evidence: In-text mention associated with Figure 1: "bilateral congenital cataract" in a Lowe syndrome case with an OCRL1 variation.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the reported patient in a disease-focused Lowe syndrome/OCRL1 article; the in-text clinical characteristics are linked to this figure and include bilateral congenital cataract plus craniofacial dysmorphism. The eyes are anonymized, so the cataract itself is not directly visible, but the patient image still visibly shows the dysmorphic facial phenotype attributable to Lowe syndrome.
